items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: And my father, we would go every week to Rochester, New York to Levitt’s Music and he would buy more stocks, whatever the popular tune was, and we’d play it.

ctx.x: Oh, well, these were dance band arrangements. They were called convertible arrangements. I called them contemptible, contemptible, but anyway these arrangements

were written for a typical society dance band which included violin; piano, bass and drums; saxophones, so you would have your first alto, your second tenor, and the third part would be baritone sometimes. All right? And two trumpets and one trombone. Usually. And they were expandable, also expendable. So you could play them with a trumpet and an alto saxophone, first trumpet and first alto, and rhythm section, and they would sound. But then you could add all those other instruments and they’d sound fuller. And…
